a1-r01.title: My Morning
a1-r01.text: I wake up at seven in the morning. I wash my face and brush my teeth. Then I eat breakfast with my family. I drink tea and eat bread and eggs. After breakfast, I go to work by bus. I start work at nine. I am happy in the morning.

a1-r02.title: My Evening
a1-r02.text: I come home at six in the evening. I cook a nice dinner for my family. We eat together at seven. After dinner, I watch TV and read a book. At ten, I take a warm shower. Then I go to bed at eleven. I sleep very well at night every day.

a1-r03.title: My Weekend
a1-r03.text: On Saturday, I do not work. I get up late at nine. I clean my house in the morning. In the afternoon, I visit my friends. We drink coffee and talk. On Sunday, I go to the park. I walk and relax. I love the weekend. It is a good time for me.

a1-r04.title: My Job
a1-r04.text: I work in an office. I am a clerk. I start work at nine and finish at five. I use a computer every day. I write emails and answer the phone. My office is big and clean. I like my job very much. My coworkers are kind. We have lunch together at noon.

a1-r05.title: My Day
a1-r05.text: I get up at six thirty. I make my bed. Then I take a shower. I eat a quick breakfast and go to work. At noon, I have lunch. In the evening, I go to the gym. I exercise for one hour. Then I go home and have dinner. I sleep at ten.

a1-r06.title: My Family
a1-r06.text: I have a small family. There are four people. My father is a teacher. My mother is a nurse. I have one brother. His name is Tom. He is ten years old. We live in a small house. We eat dinner together every day. I love my family very much.

a1-r07.title: My Mother
a1-r07.text: My mother is a very kind woman. Her name is Sara. She is forty years old. She works in a big hospital. She is a nurse. She helps sick people every day. At home, she cooks delicious food for us. She likes to read books in the evening. I love my mother. She is my best friend.

a1-r08.title: My Father
a1-r08.text: My father is tall and strong. His name is John. He is forty-five years old. He works in a school. He is a teacher. He teaches math to young students. He drives a blue car. On weekends, he plays football with me in the park. He is very kind. I like my father a lot.

a1-r09.title: My Sister
a1-r09.text: I have one sister. Her name is Lily. She is eight years old. She has long brown hair and blue eyes. She likes to draw and sing. She goes to school every day. After school, she plays with her dolls. She is very funny and happy. We play together in the garden every day.

a1-r10.title: My Grandmother
a1-r10.text: My grandmother is old and wise. She is seventy years old. She lives with us in our house. She tells nice stories every night before bed. She makes bread in the morning. The bread is very tasty and fresh. She also plants flowers in the garden. I help her every day. I love my grandmother.

a1-r11.title: My Breakfast
a1-r11.text: Every day, I eat a big breakfast. I eat bread with cheese and fresh eggs. I also eat some tomatoes and olives. I drink a cup of tea with milk. Sometimes I eat honey with bread too. Breakfast is my favorite meal. It gives me energy for the whole day at work.

a1-r12.title: My Lunch
a1-r12.text: At noon, I eat my lunch at work. I usually eat rice with chicken and salad. The salad has fresh tomatoes and cucumbers. I drink a glass of cold water. Sometimes I eat soup first. I do not eat fast food. I like healthy food very much. It is good for my body.

a1-r13.title: My Favorite Food
a1-r13.text: My favorite food is pasta. I love pasta with tomato sauce very much. My mother makes it on Sundays. She adds cheese on top. It is very delicious and hot. I also like pizza and burgers. But pasta is the best food. I can eat pasta every day of the week.

a1-r14.title: Fruits and Vegetables
a1-r14.text: I eat fresh fruit every day. I like apples, bananas, and oranges. They are sweet and healthy. I also eat many vegetables. I like carrots and spinach very much. My mother makes a big salad for dinner. Fruit and vegetables have many vitamins. They keep me strong and healthy every day.

a1-r15.title: At the Restaurant
a1-r15.text: On Friday, my family goes to a restaurant. We eat out at night. I order a burger with fries. My mother orders a green salad. My father orders a steak. We drink cold orange juice. The food is very tasty. We are all happy there. It is a fun night.

a1-r16.title: My Dog
a1-r16.text: I have a dog. His name is Rex. He is big and brown. He has long ears and a short tail. Rex likes to run in the park. He also likes to eat meat and bones. He sleeps in a small house in the garden. He is my best friend. I love Rex very much.

a1-r17.title: The Cat
a1-r17.text: My neighbor has a cat. Her name is Luna. She is a small white cat. She has blue eyes. She likes to sleep all day long. At night, she catches mice. She drinks milk every morning. She is very quiet and soft to touch. I like to play with Luna every day.

a1-r18.title: At the Zoo
a1-r18.text: The zoo is near my house. I go there with my family. We see many animals. We see big elephants and tall giraffes. We also see lions and tigers. The monkeys are very funny. They jump and play all day. I take many photos. The zoo is a fun place.

a1-r19.title: The Farm
a1-r19.text: My uncle has a farm. There are many animals on the farm. There are cows and sheep. There are also chickens and a horse. The cow gives white milk. The chickens give fresh eggs. I visit the farm in summer. I feed the animals. I like the farm very much.

a1-r20.title: Birds in My Garden
a1-r20.text: There are many beautiful birds in my garden. They are small and colorful. They sing every morning at seven. They build small nests in the tall trees. They eat seeds and small fruit. I put fresh water for them every day. They are beautiful. I like to watch the birds in the morning.

a1-r21.title: My School
a1-r21.text: My school is big, new, and nice. It has twenty classrooms and a big library. I am a student there. My teacher is Mrs. Green. She is very kind. I go to school from Monday to Friday. I study English, math, and science every week. I like my school very much.

a1-r22.title: My Classroom
a1-r22.text: My classroom is on the second floor. It is clean, bright, and quiet. There are twenty desks and chairs. There is a big white board. The walls are white. There are many posters on the walls. My desk is near the window. I sit with my very good friend Ali.

a1-r23.title: My Teacher
a1-r23.text: My English teacher is Mr. Davis. He is thirty years old. He is tall, friendly, and kind. He speaks slowly so we understand him. He always gives us fun homework. He helps every student in the class. We love his English lessons very much. He is a very good teacher.

a1-r24.title: My School Bag
a1-r24.text: I have a red school bag. It is new and big. Inside my bag, I have my books and notebooks. I also have a pencil case. There are pens and pencils in it. I have my lunch box too. My bag is heavy but I like it. I take it to school every day.

a1-r25.title: My Homework
a1-r25.text: Every day, I have homework. I do my homework in the evening. I sit at my desk and open my books. First, I do my math. Then I read a story in English. My father helps me when I need help. I finish at eight. Then I play with my dog.

a1-r26.title: My City
a1-r26.text: I live in a nice, big city. It is big and busy. There are many cars and buses on the streets. There are tall buildings and green parks. There is a big market in the center. Many people live here. I like my city very much. It is a good place to live.

a1-r27.title: The Park
a1-r27.text: There is a beautiful park in my city. It is near my house. There are many trees and flowers. There is a small lake in the park. Children play there every day. Old people walk and talk. On Sunday, I go to the park with my family. We have a picnic there.

a1-r28.title: The Market
a1-r28.text: There is a big market in my city. It opens every day at eight in the morning. There are many small shops. You can buy fresh fruit and vegetables there. You can buy bread and cheese too. The market is always busy and noisy. My mother buys food there every Saturday.

a1-r29.title: The Bus
a1-r29.text: I take the bus to work every day. The bus stop is near my house. The bus is red and big. It comes at eight fifteen. I sit near the window. I read a book on the bus. The bus is fast. I get off at the city center. The ride is twenty minutes.

a1-r30.title: My Street
a1-r30.text: My street is very quiet and clean. There are ten houses on my street. My house is number five. The houses are white and blue. There are green trees on both sides. My neighbors are friendly. Children play in the street in the evening. I like my street a lot.

a1-r31.title: The Lost Key
a1-r31.text: Mia is a small girl. She has a red key for her house. One day she loses the key. She looks in her bag and under the bed. She is sad. Then she sees the key in the garden, near the flowers. She puts the key in her pocket and smiles.

a1-r32.title: The Rain Is Coming
a1-r32.text: Tom looks at the sky. It is dark. "Rain is coming," he says. His mother puts clothes on the line. Tom runs outside and takes the clothes into the house. Then the rain comes. His mother is happy. "Thank you, Tom," she says.

a1-r33.title: A Bird in the Box
a1-r33.text: Lily finds a small box in the street. She opens it and sees a hurt bird. She takes the bird home. She gives it water and bread. Her father helps her. Every day the bird gets better. One morning the bird flies away. Lily is sad but happy.

a1-r34.title: The Hungry Cat
a1-r34.text: A small cat comes to Sam's house. It is thin and hungry. It says "meow" at the door. Sam gives it milk and bread. The cat eats and then sleeps near the warm fire. Sam wants to keep the cat. His mother says yes. Now the cat has a home.

a1-r35.title: My First Bike
a1-r35.text: Today is my birthday. My mother gives me a big box. Inside is a new blue bike. I am so happy. At first I am a little afraid. My father holds the bike. Then I can ride alone. It is a very good day.

a1-r36.title: The Little Seed
a1-r36.text: Nina gets a small seed from her teacher. She puts it in the earth and gives it water every day. The seed is quiet for many days. Nina waits and waits. Then one morning a small green leaf comes out. Nina is so happy. She tells her mother. "Your seed has a baby plant!" her mother says.

a1-r37.title: The Big Helper
a1-r37.text: Old Mrs. Green lives next door. She has a big garden. She cannot carry heavy things. One day I see her with a heavy bag. I run to her and carry the bag to her house. She smiles and says thank you. I am happy. Helping others is good.

a2-r01.title: A Weekend Trip
a2-r01.text:
Last Saturday my family and I went to the seaside.

The weather was sunny and warm. We left home early in the morning and drove for two hours. My little brother slept in the car. When we arrived, we walked on the beach and ate ice cream. I swam in the sea for a long time because the water was not cold. In the afternoon we had lunch at a small restaurant near the beach. Then we bought some souvenirs for our friends. We came home in the evening. We were all tired but very happy. I want to go there again next summer.

a2-r02.title: Going to the Airport
a2-r02.text:
My aunt lives in another country. Last week she came to visit us, so I went to the airport to meet her.

I took a bus because the airport is far from my house. The bus was full of people with big bags. At the airport I waited near the exit door. Many people came out, but I did not see my aunt. I started to worry. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my aunt! She had come out from a different door. We laughed and hugged. We took a taxi home and talked all the way.

a2-r03.title: A Day in the City
a2-r03.text:
Last Sunday I went to the city centre with my friend Ana.

We took the underground train because it is fast and cheap. First we visited the history museum. It was very interesting and we learned a lot about old times. Then we walked through the big park in the middle of the city. We bought sandwiches and sat on the grass to eat. After lunch we went shopping. Ana wanted to buy a new jacket, but she did not find one she liked. In the evening we were hungry, so we ate pizza. It was a lovely day out.

a2-r04.title: My Train Journey
a2-r04.text:
I travelled by train for the first time last month. I was a little nervous because I went alone.

I bought my ticket at the station and found my seat next to the window. The train left on time at nine o'clock. Outside the window I saw fields, rivers, and small villages. A friendly woman sat near me and we talked about our families. The journey took four hours. When I arrived, my cousin was waiting for me on the platform. He was happy to see me. Now I want to travel by train again, because it was comfortable and fun.

a2-r05.title: A Beach Holiday
a2-r05.text:
Every summer my family goes to the coast for a holiday. This year we stayed in a small hotel near the sea.

We woke up early and had breakfast on the terrace. The view of the sea was beautiful. After breakfast we went to the beach. My sister and I played in the sand and built big castles. Dad swam far out into the sea, but Mum stayed near the shore. In the evening we walked along the street and looked at the shops. We ate fresh fish for dinner. It was a wonderful holiday and I did not want to go home.

a2-r06.title: My Garden
a2-r06.text:
My favourite hobby is gardening. I have a small garden behind my house.

In spring I plant flowers and vegetables. I water them every morning before school. It is hard work, but I enjoy it because I like being outside in the fresh air. Last year I grew tomatoes and carrots. They were very tasty, and my mother used them in her cooking. My neighbour gave me some seeds for yellow flowers, and they grew well. In summer the garden is full of colour. Gardening makes me feel calm and happy. I want to have a bigger garden one day.

a2-r07.title: Playing Football
a2-r07.text:
I love playing football. I play with my friends in the park every weekend.

We are not a real team, but we play very seriously. Last Saturday we played against some boys from another street. The game was hard because the other team was fast. In the first half nobody scored a goal. Then my friend Tom passed the ball to me, and I scored. Everyone shouted and clapped. In the end we won two goals to one. After the game we were tired but happy. We all drank water and talked about the best moments of the match.

a2-r08.title: Cooking at Home
a2-r08.text:
I started cooking last year, and now it is my favourite hobby.

My grandmother taught me to cook because my parents work late. At first I could only make simple things like eggs and toast. Then I learned to cook pasta and rice. Last weekend I cooked a big dinner for my whole family. I made chicken with vegetables and a chocolate cake. Everybody said the food was delicious. My little sister helped me wash the dishes afterwards. Cooking is fun because I can try new things. I want to learn how to bake bread next.

a2-r09.title: Photography
a2-r09.text:
My hobby is taking photos. I got a camera for my birthday two years ago.

I take photos of everything I see: flowers, animals, buildings, and my friends. My favourite time to take photos is early morning, because the light is soft and beautiful. Last month I took a photo of a red bird in our garden. My father liked it so much that he put it on the wall. Sometimes I put my best photos on the internet and people leave nice comments. I want to be a photographer when I grow up, or maybe just keep it as a fun hobby.

a2-r10.title: Reading Books
a2-r10.text:
I love reading. I usually read for an hour before I go to sleep.

I like adventure stories best, because they are exciting. Last month I read a book about a boy who finds a hidden island. I could not stop reading it, so I finished it in three days. My friend Lily likes the same kind of books, so we sometimes swap our books. There is a small library near my school. I go there every Friday to choose a new book. Reading helps me learn new words, and it is also a nice way to relax after a busy day.

a2-r11.title: My Best Friend
a2-r11.text:
My best friend is called Marco. We met when we were six years old.

We live on the same street, so we walk to school together every day. Marco is tall and he has short brown hair. He is very funny and he always makes me laugh. But he is also a good friend. When I was sick last month, he brought my homework to my house and told me all the school news. We like the same music and the same computer games. I am happy that Marco is my friend. I hope we will be friends for a long time.

a2-r12.title: A Birthday Party
a2-r12.text:
Last Saturday was my friend Sara's birthday. She had a party at her house.

I arrived at four o'clock with a small gift. The house was full of balloons and colourful lights. Sara was wearing a lovely blue dress. There were about twenty people at the party. We played games in the garden and ate a lot of cake. Sara opened her presents after dinner. She was very happy when she saw my gift, a book about animals. At the end we all sang a song for her. I went home at nine o'clock feeling tired but very happy.

a2-r13.title: A New Neighbour
a2-r13.text:
A new family moved into the house next door last week. They have a son my age called Daniel.

On Sunday I saw Daniel playing alone in his garden. I was shy at first, but then I said hello. He smiled and said hello back. We started talking and I learned that he likes football and video games, just like me. We played football together until it got dark. His mother called him inside for dinner, but we agreed to meet again the next day. Now I have a new friend, and I am happy because he lives so close to me.

a2-r14.title: Studying Together
a2-r14.text:
My friend Emma and I often study together, because it is easier than studying alone.

We usually go to the library after school. We sit at a quiet table near the window. Emma is very good at maths, so she helps me with my maths homework. I am good at English, so I help her with writing. Last week we studied for a big history test for two hours every day. We asked each other questions and wrote the answers down. We both passed the test with good marks. Studying with a friend is useful, and it is also more fun.

a2-r15.title: A Phone Call
a2-r15.text:
Yesterday evening my friend Leo called me. I was surprised because he usually sends messages.

He sounded very excited and told me the news: his family is moving to my city! Leo lives far away now, so we only see each other in the summer holidays. But next month he will live only ten minutes from my house. We talked on the phone for an hour. We made plans to play basketball together and to ride our bikes to school. I am so happy. It is wonderful to know that my best friend will live near me.

a2-r16.title: At the Supermarket
a2-r16.text:
My mother and I go to the supermarket every Saturday morning.

We always make a shopping list before we go, so we do not forget anything. Mum pushes the trolley and I find the things on the list. We buy bread, milk, fruit, and vegetables. This week we also bought rice, cheese, and some chicken for Sunday dinner. The supermarket was very busy because everyone shops at the weekend. We had to wait in a long queue at the checkout. When we came home, I helped Mum carry the heavy bags into the kitchen.

a2-r17.title: Buying New Shoes
a2-r17.text:
I needed new shoes for school, so yesterday my father took me to the shoe shop.

The shop was big and had many shoes in different colours. A friendly assistant asked if she could help us. I tried on three pairs of shoes. The first pair was too small, and the second pair was not comfortable. But the third pair was perfect. They were black and very light. Dad asked about the price, and we were happy because the shoes were not expensive. He paid for them and we left the shop. I wore my new shoes to school today, and everyone said they look nice.

a2-r18.title: The Market
a2-r18.text:
There is a big market in our town every Sunday. I love going there with my grandmother.

The market is full of stalls that sell fruit, vegetables, clothes, and toys. The sellers shout to get people to buy their things, and the streets are always busy. My grandmother knows one farmer who sells the best apples. She always buys a bag of them. Last Sunday I bought a small wooden toy for my little brother. We also bought fresh bread and some cheese. The market is noisy but I love the friendly feeling there. I always look forward to Sunday.

a2-r19.title: A Gift for Mum
a2-r19.text:
It was my mother's birthday last week. I wanted to buy her a special gift.

I saved my pocket money for two months. On the day before her birthday, I went to a small shop in the town centre. I looked at many things: flowers, candles, scarves, and cups. Then I saw a beautiful blue scarf. I remembered that my mother's favourite colour is blue. The shop assistant put it in a nice box for me. When Mum opened the gift, she smiled and hugged me. She wears the scarf very often, and that makes me very happy.

a2-r20.title: Online Shopping
a2-r20.text:
My sister loves online shopping. She buys clothes, books, and shoes on the internet.

Last week she ordered a new pair of trainers. She chose the size and colour on her phone, and she paid with her card. It was very easy. The trainers arrived after three days in a big box. When she opened the box, she was a little worried because the trainers looked small. But she tried them on and they fit perfectly. She was very happy. Online shopping is fast and convenient, but sometimes it is hard to know if things will fit before they arrive.

a2-r21.title: A Rainy Day
a2-r21.text:
It rained all day yesterday. The sky was grey and the streets were wet.

I could not play outside, so I stayed at home. In the morning I read a book and watched a film with my brother. The film was about a family of bears, and it was very funny. After lunch the rain became heavier, and we could hear it on the roof. My mother made hot chocolate for us, and we drank it by the window. In the evening the rain finally stopped. I looked outside and saw a beautiful rainbow in the sky.

a2-r22.title: Snow in Winter
a2-r22.text:
Last winter we had a lot of snow. It was the best winter I can remember.

The snow started on a Friday night. When I woke up on Saturday morning, everything was white. The trees, the cars, and the roads were covered in snow. I ran outside with my sister and we made a big snowman. We gave him a carrot nose and a red scarf. Then our friends came and we had a snowball fight. It was cold, but we had so much fun. In the evening we went inside and drank warm soup. I love snowy days because the world looks so beautiful.

a2-r23.title: A Hot Summer Day
a2-r23.text:
Last summer we had some very hot days. The temperature went up to thirty-five degrees.

On the hottest day, my family went to the river to cool down. The water was cold and clear. We swam and splashed in the water all afternoon. My father brought a big umbrella, so we could sit in the shade when we were tired. We drank a lot of water and ate cold melon. It was delicious and refreshing. In the evening we had a barbecue in the garden, but it was still warm. I went to sleep with the window open, but the air was still hot.

a2-r24.title: The Weather Forecast
a2-r24.text:
Every morning my father watches the weather forecast on television before work.

Yesterday the forecast said it would be sunny, so we planned a trip to the park. We packed sandwiches and drinks and left the house early. But the forecast was wrong! In the afternoon dark clouds came, and it started to rain. We ran to a small café and waited inside. We laughed about our bad luck and ate our sandwiches there. The rain stopped after an hour, and we walked home in the fresh air. Now I know that the forecast is not always right.

a2-r25.title: A Windy Day
a2-r25.text:
Last Tuesday was a very windy day. The wind blew hard from morning until night.

On my way to school, the wind almost blew my hat away. I had to hold it with my hand. In the park, the trees moved from side to side, and dry leaves flew through the air. After school I saw that our garden was a mess. The wind had knocked over a small plant pot. I picked it up and put it back. In the evening the wind became calm, and the sky was clear. I was glad, because strong wind always makes me feel a little nervous.

a2-r26.title: Saturday Plans
a2-r26.text:
I love Saturdays because I do not have to go to school. This Saturday I have a lot of nice plans.

In the morning I will sleep a little longer, and then I will have a big breakfast. My mother is going to make pancakes. After breakfast I will play football with my friends in the park. In the afternoon I want to ride my bike to the lake with my cousin. If the weather is good, we can swim there. In the evening our family will watch a film together. I cannot wait for Saturday to come. It is going to be a great day.

a2-r27.title: A Picnic in the Park
a2-r27.text:
Next Sunday my friends and I are going to have a picnic in the park. We planned it for a long time.

Each of us will bring something to eat. I am going to bring sandwiches and juice. Lily will bring fruit, and Tom is going to bring a chocolate cake. We will meet at the park gate at eleven o'clock. After lunch we want to play badminton and throw a ball. If it rains, we will go to Lily's house instead and play board games. I hope the weather will be nice, because a picnic outside is much more fun.

a2-r28.title: Cleaning the House
a2-r28.text:
This weekend my family is going to clean the whole house. It is a lot of work, but we do it together.

On Saturday morning we will start after breakfast. My father will clean the windows, and my mother is going to wash the kitchen. My job is to tidy my room and take out the rubbish. My little brother will help by putting away his toys. It will take us about three hours. After we finish, we will order pizza for lunch as a reward. I do not really like cleaning, but I love how fresh and clean the house looks afterwards.

a2-r29.title: Visiting Grandparents
a2-r29.text:
On Saturday I am going to visit my grandparents. They live in a small village about an hour from our city.

I visit them once a month, and I always look forward to it. My grandfather has a big garden with apple trees. In the morning he will show me his new plants. My grandmother is a wonderful cook. She will make my favourite meal, chicken with rice. After lunch we will sit in the garden and drink tea. Sometimes my grandfather tells me stories about when he was young. I love spending time with them because they are kind and funny.

a2-r30.title: A Quiet Sunday
a2-r30.text:
Last Sunday I did not have any plans, and it was wonderful.

I woke up late and stayed in bed for a while. Then I made myself some toast and drank a cup of tea. I sat in the garden and listened to the birds singing. In the afternoon I read my new book and finished three chapters. Later I helped my father wash the car, and we talked about football. In the evening I watched a comedy on television with my family. It was a quiet day, but I felt relaxed and happy. Sometimes it is nice to do nothing special.

a2-r31.title: A Rainy Afternoon
a2-r31.text: My friend Mark and I were bored one rainy Saturday. We could not go outside because it was raining hard. We sat in my room and looked at the window. 'What can we do?' Mark asked. Then I remembered an old box in my cupboard. We opened it and found many old photos and toys from my childhood. We laughed at the funny photos and told stories all afternoon. When the rain stopped, we were surprised. The rainy day turned out to be one of the best days.

a2-r32.title: The Wrong Bus
a2-r32.text: I wanted to visit my grandmother, but I got on the wrong bus. I was reading and did not look at the number. After twenty minutes I looked out of the window and did not know the street. I felt nervous. I asked the driver, and he stopped the bus. He said I should get off and take the number 7 bus back. I followed his advice. When I finally arrived at my grandmother's house, she was surprised to see me so late. I told her my story, and we both laughed. Now I always check the bus number before I get on.

a2-r33.title: The Kind Neighbour
a2-r33.text: Our next-door neighbour, Mr. Ali, is a very kind man. Last winter he saw our garden full of snow. He cleaned the path to our door before my father woke up. Every morning we found the path clean. My father wanted to thank him, so he baked a cake and we took it to him. Mr. Ali smiled and said it was nothing. 'Good neighbours help each other,' he said. Now we always help him too. When I see him with heavy bags, I run to open the door.

a2-r34.title: The First Day at School
a2-r34.text: My cousin Sara moved to our city and started a new school. On her first day she was very nervous. She did not know anyone, and she ate lunch alone. In the afternoon, a girl named Elif came to her. 'Do you want to play with us?' Elif asked. Sara said yes, and they played on the playground. They talked and laughed until the bell rang. Elif walked her to the bus stop and said, 'See you tomorrow!' Sara went home with a smile. Making one friend changed her whole first day.

a2-r35.title: The Broken Bicycle
a2-r35.text: My bike broke on the way to the shop. A small stone hit the wheel and the tyre went flat. I could not ride, so I walked for twenty minutes, pushing my bike. I was upset because I wanted to be home before dinner. My older brother saw me from the window. He came out with a pump and fixed the tyre in five minutes. 'Don't worry, it is easy,' he said. I smiled and rode home behind him. I learned that problems are easier with help.

a2-r36.title: A Stormy Night
a2-r36.text: Last night a big storm came to our town. The wind was strong and the rain fell hard. Suddenly, the lights went out and our house became dark. My little sister started to cry. I took her hand and told her not to be afraid. We lit a candle and sat together near the window. My mother made hot tea and we played a quiet game. After an hour, the lights came back on. We laughed because the storm was not so bad after all. Being together made the dark night feel safe.

a2-r37.title: A Tiny Gift
a2-r37.text: On my birthday, my best friend gave me a small, plain box. I opened it and saw a ring made of old silver and a note. The note said the ring was from his grandfather. My friend said, 'My grandfather told me to give this to someone who is like family.' I put the ring on and felt something warm in my heart. It was not an expensive present, but it was the most precious one I received. I understood that a gift from the heart is worth more than money.

b1-r01.title: A Healthy Life
b1-r01.text:
Many people want to live a healthy life, but they think it is too difficult. The truth is that small changes can make a big difference. You do not need to spend hours at the gym or eat only salad every day.

Start by drinking more water instead of sweet drinks. Try to walk for thirty minutes a day, even if it is just to the shops. Go to bed at the same time each night so your body can rest. Eat more fruit and vegetables, and do not skip breakfast.

These habits are simple, but they work. After a few weeks, you will probably feel stronger and more energetic. A healthy life is not about being perfect. It is about making better choices most of the time.

b1-r02.title: Sleep Matters
b1-r02.text:
Sleep is one of the most important parts of a healthy life, but many people do not get enough of it. Adults need about seven to eight hours of sleep every night. However, busy jobs, family duties, and screens often keep us awake.

When you do not sleep enough, your body and brain cannot work well. You may find it hard to focus, and you may feel angry or sad more easily. Over time, poor sleep can even make you ill.

To sleep better, keep your bedroom dark and quiet. Stop using your phone at least half an hour before bed, because the light can stop you from feeling sleepy. Try to go to sleep and wake up at the same time every day, even on weekends.

b1-r03.title: Walking Every Day
b1-r03.text:
Walking is one of the easiest ways to stay healthy. It costs nothing, you can do it almost anywhere, and you do not need any special equipment. Doctors often say that a daily walk is good for both your body and your mind.

A regular walk can make your heart stronger and help you keep a healthy weight. It can also lower stress and make you feel calmer. Some people say that their best ideas come to them while they are walking.

You do not have to walk for hours to feel the benefits. Just thirty minutes a day is enough for most people. Try walking to work, or take a short walk after lunch. If the weather is bad, you can walk inside a shopping centre.

b1-r04.title: Eating Well at Work
b1-r04.text:
Many office workers find it hard to eat well during the day. They are busy, so they buy fast food or eat snacks at their desks. This may save time, but it is not good for their health in the long run.

Planning your meals can help. Take a few minutes each evening to prepare a simple lunch for the next day. Bring fruit or nuts to eat when you feel hungry, instead of sweets or chips. Drink water or tea instead of sugary drinks, and try not to eat while you are working.

When you eat at your desk, you often eat more than you need, because you are not paying attention to your food. It is better to take a real break and eat somewhere quiet. Your body will thank you.

b1-r05.title: Dealing with Stress
b1-r05.text:
Everyone feels stress from time to time. A little stress can even be useful, because it pushes us to work hard and meet deadlines. But too much stress is harmful. It can cause headaches, poor sleep, and a feeling of being always tired.

There are simple ways to manage stress. Exercise is one of the best, because it helps your body relax. Talking to a friend or a family member can also make you feel better; sharing a problem often makes it smaller. It also helps to make a list of the things you need to do.

Finally, remember to rest. You cannot do everything at once. Taking short breaks during the day is not a waste of time; it helps you work better.

b1-r06.title: Smartphones in Daily Life
b1-r06.text:
Smartphones have changed the way we live. With one small device, we can call our friends, send messages, take photos, and find our way around a city. Many people use their phones for banking and shopping as well.

There are, however, some problems. People often spend too much time looking at their screens, sometimes even when they are with friends and family. This can harm real relationships. Also, because the phone is always in our pocket, it is hard to switch off from work.

Experts suggest simple rules. For example, do not check your phone during meals, and put it away an hour before you sleep. Your phone is a useful tool, but it should not control your life. Using it less can make you happier.

b1-r07.title: Working from Home
b1-r07.text:
More people than ever now work from home, thanks to the internet and new technology. Many workers like this because they save time and money on travelling, and they can spend more time with their families. They also say they can focus better in a quiet room.

But working from home is not always easy. Some people feel lonely because they do not see their colleagues every day. Others find it hard to stop working, and they check emails late at night. It is also easy to become distracted by housework or the television.

The best way to work well from home is to have a plan. Start and finish at fixed times, take regular breaks, and keep a separate space just for work. Then, when you close your computer, you can truly rest.

b1-r08.title: Social Media and Friendship
b1-r08.text:
Social media allows us to stay in touch with people all over the world. We can share photos, send messages, and see what our friends are doing. For many people, especially those who live far from their families, this is a great comfort.

However, social media can also give us a false picture of friendship. We may have hundreds of online friends, but very few people we can truly talk to. Studies show that spending too much time on social media can make some people feel lonely, because everyone else seems to have a perfect life.

It is important to remember that online contact is not the same as real contact. A quick message is nice, but meeting a friend for a coffee or a walk is much more valuable.

b1-r09.title: Shopping Online
b1-r09.text:
Online shopping has become very popular in recent years. You can buy almost anything without leaving your home, and the goods arrive at your door a few days later. Prices are often lower online, and it is easy to compare different shops.

But online shopping also has some risks. Sometimes the product does not look like the photo, or the size is wrong. It can also be hard to return things, and some websites are not safe. Your personal and bank details could be stolen if you are not careful.

To shop safely online, use well-known websites and check the reviews of other buyers. Read the return policy before you pay, and never send money to a stranger. If a deal looks too good to be true, it probably is.

b1-r10.title: Staying Safe Online
b1-r10.text:
The internet is a wonderful place, full of information and fun. But just like in the real world, there are dangers online. Hackers, scams, and fake news can cause real problems if we are not careful.

The first rule of staying safe online is to use strong passwords. A good password is long and mixes letters, numbers, and symbols. You should not use the same password for everything, and you should change it from time to time. Never tell your password to anyone, even a friend.

You should also think before you click. If you receive an email from a bank asking for your details, check carefully whether it is real. Real companies never ask for your password by email. And remember that not everything you read online is true.

b1-r11.title: Plastic Waste
b1-r11.text:
Plastic is a useful material, but it has become a big problem for our planet. Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic are thrown away, and much of it ends up in the oceans. Sea animals eat small pieces of plastic, which can kill them.

One reason the problem is so large is that we use many plastic items only once. Bottles, bags, and cups are thrown away after a few minutes of use. Then they take hundreds of years to break down in nature.

We can all help to reduce plastic waste. Carry a bag when you go shopping, and say no to plastic bottles by filling your own bottle with water. Choose products with less packaging, and recycle whenever you can. Small actions by many people can make a real difference.

b1-r12.title: Saving Water
b1-r12.text:
Water is the most important thing for life, but many of us waste it without thinking. In some parts of the world, people have to walk for hours just to find clean water. Yet in other places, we leave the tap running while we brush our teeth.

Saving water is easier than you think. Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth or wash your hands. Take shorter showers instead of long baths. Fix taps that leak, because even a small drip can waste many litres over a year.

You can also save water outside the home. Water your garden early in the morning or late in the evening, so the water does not evaporate in the hot sun. If we all save a little water every day, we can protect this precious resource.

b1-r13.title: Recycling at Home
b1-r13.text:
Recycling is one of the easiest ways to help the environment. Instead of throwing things away, we can turn old materials into new products. This saves energy and reduces the amount of rubbish that goes to landfill.

Many families already recycle paper, glass, and plastic. But it is important to do it correctly. Before you put a bottle or a can in the recycling bin, rinse it and remove the lid. If the items are dirty, they may not be recycled at all.

It is also a good idea to reduce and reuse before you recycle. Buy fewer things, especially things with lots of packaging, and find new uses for old objects. A glass jar, for example, can hold pens or food. Using less in the first place is even better.

b1-r14.title: Using Public Transport
b1-r14.text:
In many cities, the air is dirty because there are too many cars on the roads. Cars produce gases that harm our health and warm the planet. Traffic is also a big problem, and drivers often waste hours sitting in jams.

Public transport can help with all these problems. A single bus can carry as many people as dozens of cars. If more people left their cars at home and used buses, trains, or trams, the air would be cleaner and the roads would be less crowded. Many cities are also making public transport cheaper.

Of course, public transport is not perfect. It can be crowded and sometimes late. But the benefits are large. Next time you need to go into town, why not try the bus or train? You might be surprised how easy it is.

b1-r15.title: Planting Trees
b1-r15.text:
Trees are very important for our planet. They give us oxygen to breathe and take in carbon dioxide, a gas that warms the Earth. They also provide homes for birds and other animals, and they stop the soil from washing away in the rain.

Sadly, forests are being cut down in many parts of the world, often to make space for farms or buildings. This is bad news for the climate and for wildlife. When trees disappear, the land becomes dry, and animals lose their homes.

But there is hope. Many people and organisations are planting trees to repair the damage. Even in cities, planting trees along streets makes the air cooler and cleaner. You can help by planting a tree in your garden or joining a local tree-planting day.

b1-r16.title: Learning a New Language
b1-r16.text:
Learning a new language is a wonderful goal, but many people give up too soon. They think they are too old, or that they do not have a special talent for languages. In fact, almost anyone can learn if they practise regularly.

The secret is to make the language part of your daily life. You do not need to sit with a grammar book for hours. Listen to songs, watch films with subtitles, and read simple stories. Try to use the new words in sentences of your own.

It is also important not to be afraid of mistakes. Nobody learns a language without making them, and every mistake teaches you something new. Speak as much as you can, even if you feel shy. The more you use the language, the more natural it will feel.

b1-r17.title: Studying Online
b1-r17.text:
Online courses have opened the door of education to millions of people. You can now learn a new skill, or even get a degree, from your own home. This is a great chance for people who work full-time or live far from a university.

Studying online has many advantages. It is often cheaper than going to a classroom, and you can study at any time of day. If you miss something, you can watch the video again. Many courses also let you learn at your own speed.

But you need self-discipline. Without a fixed timetable, it is easy to fall behind. It helps to set a regular study time and to find a quiet place without distractions. Online learning gives you freedom, but you must use that freedom wisely.

b1-r18.title: The Value of Reading
b1-r18.text:
Reading is one of the best habits you can develop. It is not only enjoyable; it also improves your mind. People who read regularly have a larger vocabulary and can express their ideas more clearly. Reading also teaches you about other people and places.

Children who read for fun often do better at school. But it is never too late to start. You can begin with short articles or easy stories and slowly move on to longer books. The kind of book does not matter as much as the habit of reading itself.

Try to read a little every day, even if it is only for ten minutes before bed. Keep a book with you, so you can read while you wait for a bus or an appointment. Over time, those small moments add up to thousands of pages.

b1-r19.title: Going to University
b1-r19.text:
For many young people, going to university is an exciting step into adult life. It is a chance to study a subject you love in depth and to prepare for a career. University is also a time to meet new people and become independent.

But university is not for everyone, and it is not the only road to success. Some people prefer to learn a trade, such as plumbing or cooking, and they can earn good money doing it. Others start their own business straight after school.

The important thing is to choose the path that fits you. Before you decide, think about what you enjoy and what kind of work you want. Talk to people who do different jobs. A university degree can open doors, but so can hard work.

b1-r20.title: Lifelong Learning
b1-r20.text:
Learning does not stop when you leave school. In fact, many people believe that education should continue through your whole life. The world changes quickly, and new skills are needed all the time. Workers who keep learning are often more successful and happier.

Lifelong learning does not have to mean going back to a classroom. You can learn a lot by reading, watching videos, or trying new things at work. Many people learn a musical instrument or a new sport simply because it gives them joy.

Learning keeps your brain active, especially as you get older. Studies suggest that people who stay curious and keep their minds busy stay healthy longer. So never think that you are too old to learn something new. Every day is a chance to grow.

b1-r21.title: My First Job
b1-r21.text:
Getting your first job is an exciting and important moment. For many people, it is the first time they earn their own money and learn what it is like to have real responsibilities. My first job was in a small cafe, and I still remember how nervous I felt.

At first, everything was difficult. I dropped cups, forgot orders, and worried that the customers were angry with me. But my colleagues were patient and helped me learn. After a few weeks, I could do the job without thinking.

That first job taught me more than how to make coffee. I learned to be on time, to work as part of a team, and to stay calm when things went wrong. These are skills I still use today. A first job may not be perfect, but it is a valuable start.

b1-r22.title: Job Interviews
b1-r22.text:
A job interview can be a stressful experience, but with good preparation you can do well. An interview is your chance to show the company who you are and why they should choose you.

Before the interview, learn about the company. Find out what it does and what the job involves. Think about the questions they may ask you, such as why you want the job and what your strengths are. It is good to prepare some questions to ask them too.

On the day, dress smartly and arrive a little early. During the interview, speak clearly and look the interviewer in the eye. Do not be afraid to take a moment to think before you answer. Remember, you are also deciding whether the company is right for you.

b1-r23.title: Working in a Team
b1-r23.text:
Most jobs today require you to work with other people. Whether you are building a house, designing a website, or running a shop, teamwork is usually part of the job. Good teams can achieve much more than one person working alone.

The key to good teamwork is communication. Team members need to share information clearly and listen to each other. It is also important to respect different opinions, even when you disagree. A good team uses the strengths of each person.

Of course, working in a team can be difficult. Sometimes people have different ideas about how to do a task, and conflicts can happen. The best way to solve a conflict is to talk calmly and look for a solution that everyone can accept.

b1-r24.title: Changing Careers
b1-r24.text:
In the past, people often did the same job for their whole life. Today, changing careers is common. People change jobs for many reasons: they want more money, better hours, or simply a new challenge.

Changing careers can be frightening, especially if you have done the same work for years. You may worry about starting again at the bottom. But a new career can also bring new energy and happiness. Many people say they wish they had changed earlier.

If you are thinking of changing careers, plan carefully. Learn about the new field, and take a course if you need new skills. Try to save some money first, so you do not feel too much pressure. A change is easier when you are prepared.

b1-r25.title: Work-Life Balance
b1-r25.text:
Finding a balance between work and the rest of your life is one of the biggest challenges of modern times. Many people work long hours and take work home with them. They answer emails late at night and think about their jobs on holiday.

Work is important, but it is not everything. Time with family and friends, hobbies, and rest are also necessary for a happy life. People who have a good work-life balance are usually healthier and more productive at work too.

To find a better balance, set clear limits. Try to leave work at a fixed time, and turn off your work phone in the evening. Say no when you already have enough to do. Remember that rest is not a reward for finishing your work; it is something you need every day.

b1-r26.title: Running a Marathon
b1-r26.text:
Running a marathon is one of the hardest things a person can do. A marathon is just over forty-two kilometres long, and finishing one takes months of training and a lot of mental strength.

Most people do not start running a marathon by accident. They begin with short runs and slowly add more distance each week. Many runners follow a training plan and run several times a week. They also rest, eat well, and sleep enough.

On the day of the race, the atmosphere is amazing. Thousands of people run through the streets while crowds cheer them on. Some runners hit a difficult moment around the thirty-kilometre mark. But those who keep going feel a huge sense of pride at the finish line.

b1-r27.title: Football Fans
b1-r27.text:
Football is the most popular sport in the world, and its fans are famous for their passion. In many countries, thousands of people go to the stadium every week to watch their team. They sing, wave flags, and celebrate every goal.

Being a football fan is about more than watching matches. Fans share a strong feeling of belonging. Supporting the same team can bring strangers together and create friendships that last a lifetime. For many people, going to a match with their father or friends is a tradition they keep for years.

However, passion can sometimes go too far, and a small number of fans cause trouble. Most supporters simply love the game. They know that in the end, it is only a game, but they still enjoy every minute of it.

b1-r28.title: The Benefits of Team Sports
b1-r28.text:
Playing a team sport is good for your body, but the benefits do not stop there. Sports like football, basketball, and volleyball teach you skills that are useful in every part of life.

When you play in a team, you learn to cooperate. You discover that the group can achieve more than one person alone, and you learn to trust others. Team sports also teach you how to win with humility and how to lose without giving up.

Playing a team sport is also a great way to make friends. You spend hours with the same people, sharing both success and failure, and strong friendships often grow from that. And of course, regular exercise keeps you fit and reduces stress. Few activities offer so many rewards.

b1-r29.title: Learning to Swim
b1-r29.text:
Swimming is a wonderful skill that everyone should learn. It is one of the few exercises that use almost every muscle in the body, and it is gentle on the joints. That is why doctors often recommend it for people of all ages.

Many adults never learned to swim as children, and they feel embarrassed about it. But it is never too late to start. Swimming lessons for adults are friendly and patient, and the teacher will help you feel safe in the water from the very first lesson.

Being able to swim is not just fun; it can also save your life. Whether you are at the beach, at a lake, or near a pool, knowing how to swim gives you confidence in the water. If you cannot swim yet, why not look for a class near you today?

b1-r30.title: Watching or Playing?
b1-r30.text:
Many people love watching sport on television. They follow their favourite teams, know the names of all the players, and never miss an important match. Watching sport is relaxing, and it can be exciting to share a big game with friends.

But watching is very different from playing. When you watch, you sit still for hours, often with snacks in your hand. When you play, you move your body, and that is what keeps you healthy. Playing sport also lets you feel the joy of scoring a goal yourself.

This does not mean you should stop watching sport. The best idea is to do both. Watch the matches you love, but make sure you also get up and play a game yourself at least once or twice a week. Your body will thank you.

b1-r31.title: The Job Interview
b1-r31.text: Nervous, I sat in the waiting room with my hands cold. This was my first real job interview, and I had prepared for weeks. I had practised my answers, ironed my best shirt, and arrived early. Then my name was called. As I walked in, I took a deep breath. The interviewer asked me questions, and at first I stumbled on my words. But I remembered my preparation and answered calmly. At the end she smiled and said, 'We will call you.' I walked out feeling lighter than I had all day. Whether or not I got the job, I had faced my fear.

b1-r32.title: The Empty Chair
b1-r32.text: My grandfather used to sit in his old armchair beside the window every evening. He told me stories about his village and read the newspaper with a cup of tea. After he passed away, the chair stayed empty. For weeks, I avoided that corner of the room because it hurt to see it. Then one evening I sat down in the chair myself. I closed my eyes and remembered his voice. The sadness did not disappear, but I felt that he was still close. Now I sit there sometimes, and I feel peaceful rather than sad.

b1-r33.title: The Difficult Decision
b1-r33.text: Maya faced a difficult choice. She had to decide between a well-paid job far from home and staying near her family with a smaller salary. Her friends said the money was worth the distance, but her heart ached at the thought of leaving. She wrote the pros and cons on a piece of paper, but neither column won. In the end, she chose the job near home. She reasoned that money comes and goes, but time with family is something she could never get back. It was not the easiest decision, but it was the right one for her.

b1-r34.title: The Unexpected Letter
b1-r34.text: One morning I found a letter in my mailbox with no sender's name. Curious, I opened it and found a dog's photo and a note. The note said: 'If you are the person who found my dog last spring, thank you. I never got to say it properly.' I stared at the note, confused. I had never owned a dog or found one. Then I remembered that my older brother had moved in briefly last spring and had talked about a lost dog. I called him, laughing. The letter was meant for him. The mix-up made us both smile and reminded us of a strange, kind spring.

b1-r35.title: The Last Train
b1-r35.text: I almost missed the last train home. I had spent the evening with friends in the city, and the time passed without my noticing. When I looked at my phone, it was later than I thought. I grabbed my coat, ran down the stairs, and reached the platform just as the doors were closing. A guard saw me and held the door open. I jumped inside, breathless and laughing. The train started to move and I found a seat, my heart still beating fast. That moment taught me to always check the time when I am having fun.

b1-r36.title: A Small Act of Courage
b1-r36.text: Today I did something small that felt big. As I left the café, I saw an old man trying to pick up bags that had fallen from his hands. Other people walked past without stopping. My first thought was to keep walking too. But I turned back, helped him gather his bags, and carried them to his car. He looked surprised and thanked me warmly. It took me less than two minutes, but I felt braver than I had in a long time. I realised that courage is often just doing one small thing when others do nothing.

b1-r37.title: The Lighthouse Keeper
b1-r37.text: Noah worked alone at a lighthouse by the sea. Some people thought his job was lonely, but Noah loved the quiet nights and the sound of the waves. His only duty was to keep the light shining so ships could find their way. One wild night, a terrible storm knocked out the electricity. Noah lit the old backup lamp and climbed to the top to keep it burning. For hours he stayed, though the wind pushed against him. At dawn, he saw a small fishing boat riding safely toward the harbour. He smiled, knowing his work had made a difference. Loneliness had never felt so meaningful.

b2-r01.title: The Rise of Remote Work
b2-r01.text:
Remote work has transformed the modern workplace. Before the pandemic, only a small minority of employees worked from home on a regular basis. Today, millions of people log in from home offices, coffee shops, and even other countries. Many workers appreciate the flexibility, saying it gives them more time with family and removes the daily commute. Employers, too, have noticed that productivity often remains stable or even improves when staff work remotely.

However, remote work also has drawbacks. Some people feel isolated without daily contact with colleagues, and the boundary between work and personal life can blur. Junior employees may miss the informal mentoring that happens naturally in an office. Despite these concerns, it seems unlikely that working from home will disappear completely. Many companies have adopted a hybrid model, allowing staff to split their time between home and the office, in an attempt to combine the best of both worlds.

b2-r02.title: The Aging Population
b2-r02.text:
Many countries are experiencing a significant demographic shift: their populations are getting older. Advances in healthcare mean that people live longer than ever before, while birth rates in many nations have fallen sharply. As a result, there are now more elderly people and fewer young workers.

This change creates several challenges for society. Pension systems, which rely on workers to support retirees, are under growing pressure. Healthcare services must adapt to treat age-related illnesses such as heart disease and dementia. At the same time, an aging population can be an opportunity. Older people often possess valuable experience and are increasingly willing to work beyond the traditional retirement age. Some governments have responded by raising the retirement age and encouraging immigration to bring in younger workers. Finding a fair balance between generations is one of the most important tasks facing modern societies.

b2-r03.title: Urbanization and City Life
b2-r03.text:
For the first time in history, more than half of the world's population lives in cities. This process, known as urbanization, is expected to continue for decades. People move to urban areas mainly for economic reasons: cities usually offer more jobs, better education, and superior healthcare.

However, rapid urban growth creates serious problems. Housing becomes expensive, and many newcomers are forced into crowded or informal settlements. Traffic congestion and air pollution reduce the quality of life, while public transport systems often struggle to keep up with demand. City planners face a difficult task. They must build affordable homes, expand transport networks, and protect green spaces, all while managing limited budgets. Some cities have embraced the idea of smart technology, using sensors and data to improve traffic flow and reduce energy use. Whether these efforts will succeed remains to be seen, but the future of humanity is, without doubt, an urban one.

b2-r04.title: The Sharing Economy
b2-r04.text:
The sharing economy has grown rapidly in the last decade. Companies such as Airbnb and Uber allow ordinary people to rent out their homes or offer rides in their cars. Supporters argue that this system makes better use of existing resources. A spare room can generate income, and a car that would otherwise sit unused can carry passengers. Consumers benefit from lower prices and greater choice.

Critics, however, point to serious problems. Traditional hotels and taxi firms complain of unfair competition, since sharing platforms are often less strictly regulated. There are also concerns about the treatment of workers, many of whom are self-employed and lack benefits such as sick pay or a pension. Local residents sometimes object when their neighbourhoods are flooded with short-term visitors. As the sharing economy matures, governments are trying to design rules that protect both consumers and workers without destroying the innovation that made these platforms popular in the first place.

b2-r05.title: Volunteering and Community
b2-r05.text:
Volunteering has long been seen as a pillar of a healthy community. Every year, millions of people give their time freely to help others, whether by tutoring children, serving food at shelters, or cleaning up local parks. The benefits of volunteering extend far beyond the people being helped. Research suggests that volunteers themselves often report higher levels of happiness and a stronger sense of purpose. It can also be a valuable way to learn new skills and meet people from different backgrounds.

However, volunteering is not without its challenges. Organisations sometimes struggle to recruit enough reliable helpers, and enthusiasm can fade when volunteers feel their efforts are not appreciated. Some critics also argue that governments use volunteers to fill gaps in public services that should be properly funded. Despite these debates, most people agree that the habit of giving time to others strengthens the social bonds that hold communities together.

b2-r06.title: Plastic Pollution in the Oceans
b2-r06.text:
Plastic pollution is one of the most serious environmental problems of our time. Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic waste end up in the oceans, where it harms wildlife and damages ecosystems. Sea creatures such as turtles, whales, and seabirds often mistake plastic bags for food, which can block their stomachs and cause death.

Over time, plastic breaks down into tiny particles called microplastics, which have been found in fish, in drinking water, and even in the human body. The problem is difficult to solve because plastic is cheap, durable, and deeply embedded in modern life. Many countries have banned single-use items such as straws and shopping bags, and some companies are developing biodegradable alternatives. Yet experts warn that such measures are not enough. Unless we dramatically reduce the amount of plastic we produce and improve recycling systems, the oceans will continue to fill with waste that takes centuries to disappear.

b2-r07.title: Renewable Energy
b2-r07.text:
As the effects of climate change become clearer, the shift towards renewable energy has accelerated. Solar panels and wind turbines now generate electricity at costs that compete with, and sometimes beat, fossil fuels. Unlike coal, oil, and gas, these sources do not produce carbon emissions, which are the main driver of global warming. Many countries have set ambitious targets to phase out fossil fuels in the coming decades.

However, the transition is not simple. The sun does not always shine, and the wind does not always blow, so renewable energy can be unreliable. Storing energy for cloudy or calm days requires batteries, which are still expensive and depend on raw materials such as lithium. Building the infrastructure also requires land and investment. Despite these obstacles, most experts believe the move to clean energy is unstoppable. The question is no longer whether the world will switch, but how quickly and fairly the transition can be achieved.

b2-r08.title: The Importance of Bees
b2-r08.text:
Bees may be small, but they play an enormous role in feeding the world. Around a third of the food we eat depends on pollination, and bees are among the most important pollinators. Without them, many fruits, vegetables, and nuts would become scarce or disappear altogether.

Unfortunately, bee populations have been declining in many parts of the world. Scientists point to several causes, including the use of certain pesticides, the loss of wildflower habitats, and diseases spread by parasites. Climate change adds further pressure by altering the seasons on which bees depend. The decline has serious economic implications, since farmers rely on bees to pollinate their crops. In response, many governments have restricted harmful chemicals, and individuals are encouraged to plant bee-friendly flowers in their gardens. Saving the bees is not just about protecting a single species; it is about safeguarding the food systems on which we all depend.

b2-r09.title: Food Waste
b2-r09.text:
Around one third of all food produced for human consumption is never eaten. This staggering amount of waste occurs at every stage of the supply chain. In developing countries, food is often lost because of poor storage and transport, while in wealthier nations it is more likely to be thrown away by shops and households. Supermarkets reject fruit and vegetables that look imperfect, and consumers buy more than they need, letting food rot in their fridges.

Food waste is not only a moral problem in a world where millions go hungry; it also harms the environment. Producing food uses land, water, and energy, all of which are wasted when the food is discarded. Rotting food in landfill sites also releases methane, a powerful greenhouse gas. Simple steps, such as planning meals, using leftovers, and relaxing cosmetic standards, could dramatically reduce the problem and save households money at the same time.

b2-r10.title: Urban Green Spaces
b2-r10.text:
Parks, gardens, and tree-lined streets are more than just pleasant places to relax. Urban green spaces provide a wide range of benefits for city dwellers. Trees absorb carbon dioxide and filter pollutants from the air, improving the quality of the air we breathe. They also provide shade, which helps to reduce the heat that builds up in concrete-heavy cities, a phenomenon known as the heat island effect.

Green spaces support wildlife, offering habitats for birds and insects that would otherwise struggle to survive in built-up areas. There are mental health benefits too: studies show that people who live near parks tend to report lower levels of stress and higher levels of well-being. Despite these advantages, green spaces are often threatened by development, since land in cities is valuable. Planners increasingly recognise, however, that preserving and creating green areas is not a luxury but a necessity for making cities healthy and liveable places.

b2-r11.title: Artificial Intelligence in Daily Life
b2-r11.text:
Artificial intelligence, or AI, is no longer a concept from science fiction. It is woven into the fabric of everyday life, often in ways we barely notice. When a streaming service recommends a film, when a smartphone predicts the words we are about to type, or when a bank detects a suspicious transaction, AI is usually working behind the scenes. These systems learn by analysing enormous amounts of data, identifying patterns that would be invisible to humans. The benefits are clear: AI can save time, improve accuracy, and help doctors detect diseases at an early stage.

However, the rapid spread of AI also raises difficult questions. Critics worry about job losses, about biases embedded in the data that train these systems, and about the lack of transparency in how decisions are made. As AI becomes more powerful, society must decide how to use it responsibly and who should be held accountable when things go wrong.

b2-r12.title: The Digital Divide
b2-r12.text:
The internet has transformed the way we learn, work, and communicate, yet access to it is far from equal. The gap between those who can use digital technology and those who cannot is known as the digital divide. This divide exists both between countries and within them. In many rural areas, reliable broadband is still unavailable, while in wealthy urban centres connection is taken for granted.

The consequences are serious. Students without internet at home struggle to complete homework and miss out on online learning. Job seekers who lack digital skills are locked out of a growing number of positions, and older people can feel excluded from services that have moved online. Closing the divide requires investment in infrastructure, affordable devices, and training programmes. Until everyone has the opportunity to participate, the benefits of the digital revolution will continue to be enjoyed by some while leaving others behind.

b2-r13.title: Smartphones and Attention
b2-r13.text:
Smartphones have put the world in our pockets, but many people worry about the price we pay for this convenience. Notifications, messages, and endless feeds are designed to capture and hold our attention. As a result, many of us find it increasingly difficult to focus on a single task for more than a few minutes. Researchers call this effect attention fragmentation, and they warn that it can reduce both productivity and the quality of our work.

The constant urge to check our phones can also disrupt face-to-face conversations and harm our sleep when we use screens late at night. Some experts recommend simple strategies to regain control: turning off non-essential notifications, keeping phones out of the bedroom, and setting aside specific times to check messages. The goal is not to abandon technology but to use it deliberately, so that our devices serve us rather than the other way round.

b2-r14.title: Cybersecurity
b2-r14.text:
As more of our lives move online, the importance of cybersecurity has grown enormously. Every day, individuals and organisations face threats from hackers who seek to steal data, money, or identities. Phishing emails, which trick people into revealing passwords, remain one of the most common forms of attack. Malware, or malicious software, can lock up computers or quietly record what users type.

The damage from a successful attack can be severe, ranging from drained bank accounts to the leaking of confidential records. Protecting ourselves requires constant vigilance. Experts recommend using strong, unique passwords, enabling two-factor authentication, and thinking twice before clicking on links in unexpected messages. Companies, meanwhile, must invest in staff training and robust security systems. In a connected world, security is not a one-time task but an ongoing habit, because attackers are always finding new ways to exploit our trust.

b2-r15.title: The Internet of Things
b2-r15.text:
The Internet of Things, or IoT, refers to the growing network of everyday objects connected to the internet. From smart thermostats that learn our schedules to fridges that order milk when supplies run low, these devices promise to make life more convenient. Sensors collect data and allow objects to communicate with each other and with us. In industry, IoT can predict when machines need repair, saving time and money. In healthcare, wearable devices can monitor a patient's heart rate and alert doctors to problems.

However, this connected world brings risks. Each device is a potential entry point for hackers, and many products have weak security. There are also privacy concerns, since smart devices gather detailed information about our habits and homes. As the number of connected devices soars into the billions, experts argue that convenience must be balanced against security, and that manufacturers must take responsibility for protecting the data their products collect.

b2-r16.title: The Gig Economy
b2-r16.text:
The gig economy, in which people take short-term jobs rather than permanent positions, has expanded rapidly. Delivery drivers, freelance designers, and online tutors are all part of this flexible workforce. For many, the appeal is obvious: gig work offers the freedom to choose when and how much to work, and it allows people to earn money without committing to a single employer. Students, parents, and those between jobs find this flexibility especially attractive.

Yet the gig economy is also controversial. Gig workers are usually classified as self-employed, which means they miss out on protections such as sick pay, holidays, and pensions that traditional employees enjoy. Their income can also be unpredictable, since there is no guarantee of work. As governments debate how to regulate this new way of working, the challenge is to preserve its flexibility while ensuring that workers are treated fairly and have a basic safety net.

b2-r17.title: Sustainable Business Practices
b2-r17.text:
Sustainability has moved from the margins to the centre of business strategy. Companies are under growing pressure from customers, investors, and regulators to reduce their environmental impact. For some, this means cutting carbon emissions or switching to renewable energy. For others, it means redesigning products so they last longer and can be recycled. The shift is not purely a matter of ethics; it can also make commercial sense. Consumers are increasingly willing to pay more for products that are responsibly made, and companies that waste less often save money on materials and energy.

However, critics warn of greenwashing, the practice of making a company seem greener than it really is through clever marketing. Genuine sustainability requires real changes throughout a business, not just a new logo or slogan. Firms that embrace it honestly may gain a competitive advantage, while those that only pretend risk losing the trust of increasingly sceptical consumers.

b2-r18.title: The Rise of E-commerce
b2-r18.text:
Online shopping has revolutionised the retail industry. In the past, buying something usually meant travelling to a physical store, but today millions of people order everything from groceries to furniture with a few taps on a screen. E-commerce offers undeniable advantages: it is convenient, often cheaper, and available around the clock. Shoppers can compare prices instantly and read reviews from other customers before making a decision. For small businesses, selling online opens up a national or even global market that would once have been out of reach.

The rise of e-commerce has, however, come at a cost. Many traditional shops have closed as customers moved online, leaving empty buildings on high streets. The environmental impact of packaging and fast delivery is also a growing concern. Retail is now a hybrid world, and the most successful companies are those that manage to combine a strong online presence with a memorable in-store experience.

b2-r19.title: Corporate Social Responsibility
b2-r19.text:
Corporate social responsibility, often shortened to CSR, refers to the idea that companies should do more than simply make a profit. According to this view, businesses have obligations to their employees, their communities, and the environment. A company practising CSR might reduce its pollution, donate to local charities, or ensure that its suppliers pay fair wages. In recent years, CSR has become a major part of corporate life, with many large firms publishing annual reports on their social and environmental performance.

Supporters argue that this is good for business as well as for society: responsible companies can attract better staff, win customer loyalty, and avoid costly scandals. Sceptics, however, claim that much CSR is little more than public relations, designed to improve a company's image without changing its core behaviour. The debate continues, but one thing is clear: companies are now judged not only on what they earn, but on how they behave.

b2-r20.title: Startups and Failure
b2-r20.text:
Starting a business is often romanticised, but the reality is harsh: a large proportion of startups fail within their first few years. There are many reasons for this. Some founders build a product that nobody actually wants, while others run out of money before their idea can take off. Poor management, fierce competition, and bad timing can all play a part.

Interestingly, many successful entrepreneurs have failed before, sometimes more than once. In places like Silicon Valley, failure is often seen not as a mark of shame but as a valuable learning experience. Investors frequently prefer founders who have survived a setback, because they have learned what does not work. The lesson is that failure is not necessarily the opposite of success but often a step on the road towards it. What matters is the ability to analyse mistakes, adapt, and try again with better judgement.

b2-r21.title: The Decline of Print Newspapers
b2-r21.text:
For more than a century, newspapers were the main source of news for most people. Today, however, the print newspaper is in steep decline. Circulation has fallen in almost every country as readers have moved online, where news is free and instantly updated. Advertising, which once provided most of a newspaper's income, has also migrated to digital platforms such as search engines and social media. As a result, many papers have closed or drastically reduced their staff, and local journalism has been hit especially hard.

Some publications have adapted by introducing paywalls, charging readers a subscription to access articles online. Others have tried to survive through sponsored content or events. The decline of print raises an important question: if reliable journalism requires money, and free online news undermines that income, how will society fund the reporting that holds power to account? The answer is still unclear.

b2-r22.title: Social Media and News
b2-r22.text:
For a growing number of people, social media has become the primary way of receiving news. Platforms such as Facebook and X deliver a constant stream of headlines, videos, and opinions directly to our phones. This shift has obvious advantages: news reaches people quickly, and ordinary citizens can share events as they happen.

Yet the rise of social media as a news source has also created serious problems. Algorithms are designed to show us content that keeps us engaged, which often means content that confirms what we already believe. This can trap users in echo chambers, where they rarely encounter opposing viewpoints. Worse still, false stories spread faster than true ones, because sensational claims attract more clicks. Experts urge users to check sources, question headlines, and follow a variety of outlets. In an age of information overload, the ability to tell fact from fiction has become an essential skill.

b2-r23.title: Streaming and Television
b2-r23.text:
The way we watch television has changed beyond recognition. Not long ago, families gathered at a fixed time to watch programmes on a handful of channels. Today, streaming services such as Netflix and Disney+ allow us to watch whatever we want, whenever we want, on almost any device.
